title: Not Ray Brown: Sam's own style with Peterson and polls
summary: Sam told writers he was no Ray Brown, and his style helped the trio win its first group poll.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Just like I was saying before, that's what bothers me about it because I resent the fact that somebody is going to try to compare me to you or you to Richard Davis or to Ron Carter or anybody else that we want to name. I mean because I respect you and what you do and I listened to you and have always respected and loved what you do because I respect your individuality and I hold it in that regard. I don't listen to you saying man we should have done that like Ray Brown did or Oscar Pettiford did. No, damn that. I think that's bullshit. I mean I've got to listen to you, what you with your consummate feelings and mentality and how

you feel about music, about how you as a painter, I mean like when you paint your pictures with your instrument and your music, how you feel about music, th at's what's important to me not just sit up and try to say he didn't quite do it like somebody else. To me that's a bunch of crap.
It sure is. That's the way I feel about it. I remember when that was brought, dropped on me when I first joined the Oscar Peterson trio.

Yeah because I heard people trying to say, you know going to try to compare your music, some of th ese writers are going to try to compare how Oscar sounded with you in the band as opposed to Ray Brown and try to compare it. Because I had to rain on a couple of dudes once, I almost went to blows.
I told the writers right then and there, I said look here, man, I'm no Ray Brown and ain't trying to be.
And I'm going to play like I play. I ain't thinking about no Ray Brown.
Like I said I think in the last interv:ew we had last week, my style of playing changed his style of playing.
Where he had never won a poll as a group in his whole career ......... (unintelligible) won the Playbopoll as a group, you see.
Before he had never won as a group, you see. Individuals winning polls, maybe he'd win the piano poll or Ray Brown would win the bass poll.
It looked like Ray Brown won the bass poll for about the last 20 years. That was his thing. And I don't think that was fair because that showed me that there wasn't nobody listening at nobody else.
Because I always wondered how much Norman Granz was behind all that.
See, just write a check man, write a check. And that would straighten out all of that stuff.
